_note: The Discover Crete quote (DECISIONS.md D-005). A traditional, anonymous Cretan mantinada TAKEN from a published folk collection — never composed. Every field below was read off the page scans themselves, not off the OCR text: the OCR of this page is wrong in the second line (it cannot be trusted to have read 'χλωρὸν τυρὶ', fresh cheese). The page prints a monotonic transcription of the 1876 polytonic setting; `asPrinted` keeps the original. There is no English rendering on the page — a translation would be composition, and the Greek corpus is the owner's to sign off. `gloss` is for the owner's reading only and is not rendered.
lines: Να 'χα τη θάλασσα κρασί και τα καράβια κούπα
Και τα βουνά χλωρόν τυρί και την αγάπ' απού 'χα.
cite: Άσματα κρητικά μετά διστίχων και παροιμιών, εκδ. Anton Jeannaraki, Λειψία 1876, σ. 277, αρ. 153
asPrinted: Νά 'χα τὴ θάλασσα κρασὶ καὶ τὰ καράβια κοῦπα
Καὶ τὰ βουνὰ χλωρὸν τυρὶ καὶ τὴν ἀγάπ' ἀποῦ 'χα.
transcription: Polytonic to monotonic only: breathings and graves dropped, circumflex to acute, the accent removed from the monosyllable Νά. Spelling, dialect forms (χλωρόν, απού) and punctuation are the book's.
gloss: If only I had the sea for wine and the ships for cups, the mountains for fresh cheese, and the love I had.

source.editor: Anton Jeannaraki (Αντώνιος Ιαννάρακης) — the name as printed on the title page
source.title: Ἄσματα κρητικὰ μετὰ διστίχων καὶ παροιμιῶν / Kretas Volkslieder nebst Distichen und Sprichwörtern, in der Ursprache mit Glossar
source.section: Μαντινάδες (pp. 259–290 per the book's own table of contents)
source.catalogue: Oxford University copy, digitised by Google Books (id 3AILAAAAQAAJ); archive.org status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT
source.copyright: Anonymous traditional verse, published 1876. Public domain.
source.verified: 2026-09-11, against the page scan (leaf 291) and the title page (leaf 7)

why: Chosen for Discover Crete because it is Crete as a table: the sea, the ships, the mountains, the island's own cheese and wine — hospitality in fifteen syllables a line, and the one couplet in the section whose whole subject is the landscape the villas look at.
